configurations.label: overdamped Brownian dynamics of spherical tracers in an implicit solvent, undriven. Mass-based time units do not enter: in the overdamped limit they are absent from the physics and have no experimental counterpart (5.7). A7 abstains here rather than being pruned -- this configuration drives nothing, and the a7 card says so (4.5.3)

dimensions.why: Three, which every run under this configuration has assumed and which its tracer diffusivity was verified against. Stated now rather than left implicit: it was implicit and estimator.py hardcoded 3 to match, which was right here and wrong for four of the five configurations declared beside it.

output_independent_of_input.why:
The tracer diffusivity is fixed analytically by the input, so a run of this configuration confirms the integrator and the estimator and says nothing independent about any diffusivity (5.3). A card wanting that number cites the input, not the run. A configuration with interactions or confinement would declare true.

The claim is about the physics and not about the backend: D = k_BT/(3*pi*eta*d) is pinned by the inputs, so whichever engine integrates it, the output is determined by what went in. It therefore survives the move to HOOMD unchanged.

THE EVIDENCE BELOW IS THE MOCK'S. run-20260920-001 gave 2.128e-13 against the analytic 2.146e-13, 0.8 per cent, on mock_backend. It is labelled rather than restated because a number that stops saying which engine produced it is the same defect `executed_by` exists to prevent. A hoomd_backend run either earns this figure again on that engine, or this sentence keeps saying whose it is.

executed_by.why:
Moved 2026-09-22, after the engine ran. hoomd_backend on HOOMD 7.2.0 carried revision 3 at three seeds -- run-20260922-hoomd-s1b, -s2, -s3 -- against the analytic 8.58440e-14 m^2/s: ratios 1.00078, 1.00107, 0.99958, mean 1.00047, spread 0.15 per cent. Checked against the ANALYTIC and not against the mock, because two implementations of one closed-form relation agreeing is the same circularity one layer out (5.3). mock_backend also ran revision 3 at three seeds and stays a first-class backend (4.6.5); this field names what the declared engine is, not the only thing that may run.

THE FIRST EXECUTION AND THE FIRST CORRECT RECORD ARE TWO DIFFERENT RUNS, and the pair is kept rather than tidied. run-20260922-hoomd-s1 is the first time the engine ran and its log says `backend: mock_backend`. operator recorded it with getattr(backend, 'NAME', mock_backend.NAME) and NEITHER backend class had NAME -- so that getattr had never once succeeded and the default was the only path it ever took. Correct while the mock was the only backend, false the first moment it was handed another. Had it stood, a mock-versus-engine comparison would have read two mock runs, and this field would have been moved on that.

It was caught because the NUMBERS disagreed with the label: -s1's diffusivity and standard error did not match the mock run it claimed to be. Both runs are kept and the pair is the evidence rather than the claim -- normalise the volatile fields and -s1 and -s1b differ only in `backend`, with observables.json and trajectory_meta.json identical, so the label was the single error and the engine is deterministic in its seed. Verified here from disk: both read D = 8.591092e-14 and rel_se = 1.760e-05.

Why this field existed: `devices` named hoomd_backend while every run was the mock's, caught by simulation-2 on 2026-09-21. Today the two agree for the first time. The field stays anyway, because what it holds now is which engine produced the evidence above -- and the -s1 incident is what a reader needs to not trust a backend label that nothing derives.

temperature_realisation.why:
Temperature enters as a parameter of the noise amplitude and there is no mechanism that could fail to realise it: no velocity is represented, so there is no kinetic energy and nothing to thermostat. Same reason mass-based time units do not enter the overdamped limit (5.7), which this configuration's label already says.

TRUE OF BOTH BACKENDS, and each for its own code rather than by assumption. mock_backend integrates a position-only Wiener increment, positions + normal(0, sqrt(2*D*dt)) with D = k_B*T/(3*pi*eta*d). hoomd_backend uses hoomd.md.methods.Brownian, whose own comment at src/hoomd_backend.py:373 says 'Brownian and not Langevin: the overdamped limit is the model' -- Brownian dynamics integrates positions and does not carry velocities. Verified against the installed HOOMD 7.2.0.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: hoomd.md.methods.Langevin carries velocities and a thermostat that can lose its setpoint at large dt or to a flying ice cube, and `kind` would become `thermostat` -- a claim that is empirical and falsifiable where this one is not. So a configuration switching method switches which confirmation it owes, which is why this is a declared field and not prose. Measured from the code by simulation-2 for the mock and by manager-simulation for the engine; architecture asked for the second half on 2026-09-22 after noting the justification named one implementation.

configurations.label: overdamped Brownian dynamics in two dimensions, periodic, with a purely repulsive Yukawa pair potential (screened Coulomb, no attractive well), undriven. A7 abstains: this configuration drives nothing.

dimensions.why: Two, as the label says and as the person fixed on 2026-09-23. The psi6 bond-orientational order parameter this configuration produces is a two-dimensional quantity.

output_independent_of_input.why: Unlike bd_overdamped, the output is NOT fixed analytically by the inputs. How long a Yukawa suspension takes to order from a random start is not a closed form in the prefactor and screening length, so a run is evidence about the model and not a check of the integrator.

configurations.label: a single active Brownian particle in two dimensions with no pair interaction, no wall and no obstacle: one orientation diffusing at D_R, self-propulsion v0 along it, translational noise D_T, unwrapped coordinates. A7 abstains.

dimensions.why: Two, as the label says. It enters the estimator twice over -- through D = slope/(2*d) and through the persistence time 1/((d-1)*D_R), which is 1/D_R in two dimensions and 1/(2*D_R) in three.

output_independent_of_input.why: FALSE, and this is the field a reader is most likely to get wrong here. The mean squared displacement of a NON-INTERACTING active Brownian particle is a closed form in v0, D_R and D_T, so a sweep of this configuration confirms the integrator, the estimators and the crossover machinery and measures no dependence. It is worth running for exactly that and a card must not cite it as evidence about the dependence itself. Interaction or confinement flips this to true -- abp_wca_2d declares true for that reason.

configurations.label: one overdamped particle, no pair interaction, in an external harmonic potential of stiffness k_t, with the background fluid moving at constant velocity relative to the trap. DRIVEN: A7 stops abstaining and owns the flow speed and direction.

dimensions.why: Three, and DECLARED BY THIS SEAT RATHER THAN READ OFF A CARD -- the question's cards state no dimensionality anywhere. It follows bd_overdamped, which this configuration is one trap and one flow away from: a bead in water with three-dimensional thermal motion, whose drag offset is then resolved along the flow axis. The execution seat should say so if its plan assumes otherwise, because this field is now what the estimator divides by.

output_independent_of_input.why: FALSE for the same reason as bd_overdamped: the steady-state offset is gamma*v/k_t and the estimator inverts the very balance the integrator solved, so k_t comes out because it went in. What a run of this configuration CAN establish is the precision of the recovery, and the stiffness cancels there -- signal gamma*v/k_t and standard error sigma*sqrt(2*tau/T) both go as 1/k_t, so SE/signal = sqrt(2*D/T)/v is independent of stiffness. That is falsifiable and is why the sweep exists.
